item.title: Remember When: Dennis Hopson Scores 32 Points in Ohio State's Win Over Kentucky in the First Round of the 1987 NCAA Tournament
item.description: A day after former Ohio State coach Woody Hayes passed away, Dennis Hopson did what he did best: Score plenty of points while leading the Buckeyes to a win. item.title: Ohio State Falls to No. 1 Seed UCLA, 72-62, in Big Ten Tournament Semifinals
item.description: Ohio State’s Big Ten Tournament run ended with a semifinal loss to UCLA for the second year in a row. After beating Indiana and Minnesota in their first two games of Big Ten Tournament play, the Buckeyes (26-7) were unable to dethrone the conference’s top team on Saturday, falling 72-62 to No. 1 seed UCLA (30-1) in the semifinals. item.title: Press Coverage: Bruce Thornton Makes History in Fitting Fashion As Ohio State Positions Itself to Make First NCAA Tournament in Four Years
item.description: It was a historic and drought-ending night for Ohio State men’s basketball in the Buckeyes’ regular-season finale. In front of a sellout crowd at the Schottenstein Center, Bruce Thornton became Ohio State’s all-time leading scorer, breaking Dennis Hopson’s all-time record of 2,096 points with a 3-pointer late in the first half. item.title: Ohio State Earns No. 8 Seed, Double-Bye in Big Ten Tournament
item.description: Ohio State's Big Ten Tournament position is set. With Ohio State beating Indiana and UCLA beating USC on Saturday night, the Buckeyes are locked in as the No. 8 seed heading into the conference tourney. They beat out Iowa by one game for the final double-bye spot. Ohio State will play its first game of the Big Ten Tournament on Thursday, facing the winner of the ninth-seeded Hawkeyes and the winner of the No. 16 vs. No. 17 seed game between Oregon and Maryland. item.title: Ohio State Wrestlers Jesse Mendez and Ben Davino Win Big Ten Titles, Buckeyes Finish Second in Team Standings
item.description: Ben Davino and Jesse Mendez are Big Ten champions. Ohio State’s 133 and 141-pound wrestlers won their divisions on Sunday, leading the Buckeyes to a second-place finish at the Big Ten championships. In a battle of future Big Ten stars, Davino defeated Penn State’s Marcus Blaze in a tiebreaker. Blaze went 19-0 in the regular season with a 15-0 record in duals, but Davino took him the distance, beating the NCAA’s top-ranked 133-pound wrestler via riding time in the second tiebreaker period. 133 |
